accuracyFlags.claim: Section 07: 'At intersections, the current rule is that a turning vehicle gives way to one going straight through. Guidance published before 2012 says the opposite and is still widely circulated, so ignore anything that does not match this.'
accuracyFlags.correct: Turning-gives-way-to-not-turning is a long-standing rule, not a 2012 change. The 25 March 2012 changes were: (1) a driver turning right gives way to oncoming traffic turning left (same or no signs/signals, including green light); (2) at an uncontrolled T-intersection, traffic on the stem gives way to all traffic on the through road ('top of the T'), also at uncontrolled driveways. Roundabouts unchanged. Suggested: 'If you are turning, give way to all vehicles that are not turning. If you are turning right, also give way to oncoming vehicles turning left. Since 25 March 2012 this applies even when both of you face the same sign or signal. At an uncontrolled T-intersection, traffic on the top of the T goes first. Older guidance from before March 2012 gets these last two rules wrong.'

Rewrite to the NZTA wording and link nzta.govt.nz/roadcode give way rules.
